description: Top 50 questions d'entretien POO (Programmation Orientée Objet) : classes, objets, encapsulation, héritage, polymorphisme, abstraction.

questions.answer_text: OOP (Object Oriented Programming) is a system in which programs are considered as a collection of objects. Each object is nothing but an instance of a class.

questions.prompt: What are the basic concepts of OOP?
questions.answer_text:
The four concepts of OOP are:
1. Abstraction
2. Encapsulation
3. Inheritance
4. Polymorphism
A class is simply a representation of a type of object. It is the blueprint / plan / template that describes the details of an object.
An object is an instance of a class. It has its own state, behavior, and identity.

Encapsulation is an attribute of an object, and it contains all data which is hidden. That hidden data can be restricted to the members of that class. Access levels are Public, Protected, Private, Internal, and Protected Internal.
Polymorphism is assigning behavior or value in a subclass to something that was already declared in the main class. Simply put, polymorphism means taking more than one form.

Inheritance is a concept where one class shares the structure and behavior defined in another class. If inheritance is applied to one class it is called Single Inheritance; if it depends on multiple classes, it is called Multiple Inheritance.
Manipulators are functions which can be used in conjunction with the insertion (<<) and extraction (>>) operators on an object. Examples are endl and setw.

A constructor is a method used to initialize the state of an object, and it gets invoked at the time of object creation.

Rules for a constructor:
- The constructor name should be the same as the class name.
- A constructor must have no return type.
A destructor is a method which is automatically called when the object goes out of scope or is destroyed. The destructor name is the same as the class name but with a tilde (~) symbol before it.
An inline function is a technique used by the compiler that instructs it to insert the complete body of the function wherever that function is used in the program source code.

A virtual function is a member function of a class whose functionality can be overridden in its derived class. It is declared using the keyword 'virtual' during function declaration. In C++ it uses the 'virtual' token; in C/Python it can be achieved using function pointers.

A friend function is a friend of a class that is allowed to access public, private, or protected data in that same class. A friend can be declared anywhere in the class declaration, and it is not affected by access control keywords like private, public, or protected.

Operator overloading is a function where different operators are applied depending on the arguments. Operators like +, -, * can be passed through the function, and each has its own precedence to execute.

An abstract class is a class which cannot be instantiated. Creating an object is not possible with an abstract class, but it can be inherited. Java allows only abstract methods in an abstract class, while other languages allow non-abstract methods as well.
The ternary operator is an operator which takes three arguments. It is also called a conditional operator. (condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse)

questions.prompt: What is the use of the finalize method?
questions.answer_text: The finalize method helps to perform cleanup operations on resources which are no longer used. The finalize method is protected, and it is accessible only through this class or by a derived class.

questions.prompt: What are the different types of arguments (Call by Value vs Call by Reference)?
questions.answer_text:
A parameter is a variable used when declaring a function; arguments are passed to the function body and must match the parameter defined.

- Call by Value: the value passed is modified only inside the function; the original value stays unchanged.
- Call by Reference: the value passed is modified both inside and outside the function.

The super keyword is used to invoke the overridden method of a superclass. It allows access to overridden methods and to hidden members of the superclass. It also forwards a call from a constructor to a constructor in the superclass.

Method overriding is a feature that allows a subclass to provide the implementation of a method already defined in the main class. It overrides the superclass implementation by providing the same method name, same parameters, and same return type.
An interface is a collection of abstract methods. If a class implements an interface, it inherits all the abstract methods of that interface. Java uses interfaces to implement multiple inheritance.

An exception is an event that occurs during the execution of a program. Exceptions can be of any type — runtime exceptions or error exceptions. They are handled through an exception handling mechanism using try, catch, and throw keywords.

A token is the smallest element a compiler recognizes; it cannot be broken down further. Keywords, identifiers, constants, string literals, and operators are examples of tokens. Even punctuation characters (brackets, commas, braces, parentheses) are considered tokens.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between overloading and overriding?
questions.answer_text: Overloading is static binding, whereas overriding is dynamic binding. Overloading is the same method name with different arguments in the same class. Overriding is the same method name with the same arguments and return type across a class and its child class.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between a class and an object?
questions.answer_text: An object is an instance of a class. Objects hold information, but classes don't hold data themselves — they define properties and functions used by objects. A class can have sub-classes, while an object doesn't have sub-objects.

Abstraction shows only the necessary details to the client of an object, hiding the inner implementation. Example: to switch on a television you don't need to know the inner circuitry — only the essential controls are exposed.
Access modifiers determine the scope from which a method or variable can be accessed. There are five types: Private, Protected, Public, Friend, and Protected Friend.
Sealed modifiers are access modifiers where the method cannot be inherited. They can also be applied to properties, events, and methods. This modifier cannot be used on static members.

questions.prompt: How can we call the base method without creating an instance?
questions.answer_text: Yes, it is possible: the base method must be a static method, or you do inheritance from that class and use the 'base' keyword from a derived class.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between new and override?
questions.answer_text: The 'new' modifier instructs the compiler to use the new implementation instead of the base class function. The 'override' modifier overrides the base class function.

questions.prompt: What are the various types of constructors?
questions.answer_text:
There are three types:
- Default Constructor — with no parameters.
- Parametric Constructor — with parameters; creates a new instance while passing arguments.
- Copy Constructor — creates a new object as a copy of an existing object.

questions.prompt: What is early and late binding?
questions.answer_text: Early binding refers to assigning values to variables during design/compile time, whereas late binding refers to assigning values to variables during run time.
The 'this' pointer refers to the current object of a class. It differentiates the current object from the global object — it always refers to the current object.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between structure and a class?
questions.answer_text: The default access type of a structure is public, but for a class it is private. A structure is used for grouping data, whereas a class groups data and methods. Structures are used mainly for data without strict validation; classes encapsulate and inherit data and require strict validation.

questions.prompt: What is the default access modifier in a class?
questions.answer_text: The default access modifier of a class is Internal, and the default access modifier of a class member is Private.

questions.prompt: What is a pure virtual function?
questions.answer_text:
A pure virtual function can be overridden in the derived class but cannot be defined in the base class. It is declared using the operator = 0.

Example :
virtual void function1();      // Virtual, not pure
virtual void function2() = 0;  // Pure virtual

questions.prompt: What are the operators that cannot be overloaded?
questions.answer_text:
The following operators cannot be overloaded:
1. Scope Resolution (::)
2. Member Selection (.)
3. Member selection through a pointer to function (.*)

Dynamic or runtime polymorphism is also known as method overriding, in which a call to an overridden function is resolved during runtime, not at compile time. It means having two or more methods with the same name and same signature but different implementations.

questions.prompt: Do we require a parameter for constructors?
questions.answer_text: No, we do not require a parameter for constructors.
A copy constructor is a special constructor for creating a new object as a copy of an existing object. There is always only one copy constructor, defined either by the user or by the system.

questions.prompt: What does the keyword 'virtual' represent in a method definition?
questions.answer_text: It means we can override the method.

questions.prompt: Can a static method use non-static members?
questions.answer_text: No (False). A static method cannot use non-static members.

questions.prompt: What are a base class, subclass, and superclass?
questions.answer_text: The base class is the most generalized class (the root class). A subclass is a class that inherits from one or more base classes. The superclass is the parent class from which another class inherits.

questions.prompt: What is static and dynamic binding?
questions.answer_text: Binding is the association of a name with a class. Static binding associates a name with the class during compilation time (also called early binding). Dynamic binding associates a name with the class during execution time (also called late binding).

questions.prompt: How many instances can be created for an abstract class?
questions.answer_text: Zero. You cannot create an instance of an abstract class.

questions.prompt: Which keyword can be used for overloading?
questions.answer_text: The 'operator' keyword is used for overloading.

questions.prompt: What is the default access specifier in a class definition?
questions.answer_text: The Private access specifier is used by default in a class definition.

questions.prompt: Which OOP concept is used as a reuse mechanism?
questions.answer_text: Inheritance is the OOP concept used as a reuse mechanism.

questions.prompt: Which OOP concept exposes only the necessary information to the calling functions?
questions.answer_text: Encapsulation.
